profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, labeled True North Data Centers, marks the broader industrial land use area of a data center campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, that county own zoning and permitting records identify by the project name True North Data. Loudoun County zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003, filed under that project name, rezoned roughly 105 acres to Planned Development-Office Park specifically to allow data center uses, and was approved January 18, 2018. The underlying parcel, county PIN 194103673000, covering roughly 97 acres, is recorded under a condominium-regime plat named True North Land Condo, a legal structure commonly used to subdivide one large hyperscale campus parcel into separately titled buildings, consistent with the several individual building addresses mapped elsewhere within this same cluster on and near Thunderball Drive. A 2019 grading permit for a project called True North 2 described three data center buildings with utilities, and a 2023 stormwater permit for True North Data Phase 2A covered a further 16.5 acres of disturbed area, indicating a phased expansion that continued with four tenant fit-up zoning permits issued across April and May 2025. No document reviewed this session gives a total megawatt capacity, final building count, or total square footage for the completed campus, and the identity of the corporate entity that actually filed the original 2017 rezoning application is not exposed in the county public zoning-case layer, so True North Data Solutions, the name this record carries as operator, could not be independently confirmed as a registered company through the Virginia State Corporation Commission this session. Loudoun County is widely described as the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and this record broad land-use tag reflects that scale even though the county public data does not expose a single aggregate size figure for this specific campus.

reading.body:
True North Data is a multi-building campus on roughly 97 acres in Loudoun County, Virginia, approved for development in January 2018 under zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003. The operator has not published a total megawatt capacity, final building count, or total square footage for the completed campus. Permit records from 2019 to 2025 document phased construction of at least three data center buildings, with four tenant fit-up permits issued in April and May 2025, indicating ongoing buildout, but the campus capacity and configuration remain opaque from public sources.

The operator's name, True North Data Solutions, could not be verified as a registered Virginia corporation this session, and the company's website redirects to a domain-for-sale page. This lack of verification does not confirm whether the operator is inactive or simply maintains no published web presence. Without published specifications, True North Data cannot be ranked among Virginia's published-capacity facilities, though it is mapped as one of 326 data center sites in the state and sits within Loudoun County, which holds 23 facilities with published capacity totaling 1375.4 MW and is widely recognized as the largest data center market in the world.

Whether True North Data matters to AI scaling depends on the final capacity of its build-out, which is not published. The size of the approved land, the multi-year permit timeline, and the recent tenant fit-ups suggest a substantial campus under construction, but without operator-published megawatt figures, power draw, or power supply agreements with the Virginia grid, this facility's contribution to AI compute capacity cannot yet be quantified from the data available to this site.
